title: Karl Marx and Capitalism's Critics
objective: After this level you can explain Marx's critique of capitalism and how far it spread.
summary: Marx argued owners keep the value workers create as profit and predicted workers would overthrow capitalism. Communism once ruled a third of the world; critics rejected his theory of value.

cards.headline: Smith saw a town fed by self-interest. Marx saw workers being shortchanged.
cards.body: In 1848, Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels published The Communist Manifesto. In 1867 came the first volume of Das Kapital. Marx's question: who really creates the value in what a factory makes, and who keeps it?

cards.headline: Where does profit come from?
cards.body: Marx built on concepts inherited from Adam Smith and David Ricardo, including the labor theory of value: a product's value is set by the labor it takes to make it. Follow that through and profit looks suspicious. If workers create the value, but owners pay them just enough to live on and keep the rest, that leftover is what Marx called surplus value. To him, profit rested on exploitation.

cards.headline: A prediction of revolution
cards.body: Marx saw history as a series of class struggles, and under capitalism that meant owners of capital against workers. He expected wealth to pile up in fewer hands, and he and Engels predicted the industrial working class would one day overthrow capitalism. He pictured that revolution in industrialized countries. The revolution that did come was in mostly agrarian Russia, under Lenin's version of his ideas.

cards.fact: For much of the 20th century, about a third of the world lived under communist governments.
cards.context: Leaders including Lenin and Mao built on Marx's writings to impose communism on more than twenty countries, and his ideas inspired labor and socialist movements in western Europe. Critics went after the foundation. The Austrian school argued that a thing's value comes from its ability to satisfy wants, not the labor used to make it, and labor itself varies so much in skill that value is hard to measure that way.

mascot.line: Same starting point as Smith, opposite conclusion. Economics is like that sometimes.

cards.headline: Marx's critique
learned: Marx held that labor creates value
Owners keep the surplus as profit, he argued
He predicted workers would overthrow capitalism
Critics rejected his labor theory of value

questions.prompt: In Marx's theory, what is surplus value?

options.label: The value workers create beyond their wages, kept as profit
Money a government prints beyond what it needs
options.rationale: That's a different worry; Marx's surplus came from labor.

options.label: Goods left unsold at the end of the year
options.rationale: Surplus value is about wages and profit, not leftover stock.

options.label: The interest a bank pays on savings
options.rationale: Marx tied surplus value to workers and owners, not banks.

questions.explanation: Marx argued owners pay workers less than the value their labor adds and keep the difference, surplus value, as profit.

questions.prompt: Why did Austrian-school critics reject the foundation of Marx's theory?

options.label: They thought workers should be paid nothing
options.rationale: Their objection was about where value comes from.

options.label: They argued value comes from how well a thing satisfies wants, not labor
They believed only gold has real value
options.rationale: That was not their argument against Marx.

options.label: They said factories create no value at all
options.rationale: They located value in wants, not in denying production.

questions.explanation: The Austrian school held that value comes from a thing's ability to satisfy wants, which contradicts the labor theory of value.

questions.prompt: Marx built on concepts from earlier economists. Which Level 91 thinker was one of them?

options.label: Milton Friedman
options.rationale: Friedman came long after Marx; you met him in Level 6.

options.label: Satoshi Nakamoto
options.rationale: Bitcoin's creator appeared in 2008, over a century after Marx.

options.label: R. A. Radford
options.rationale: Radford described Level 1's prison camp in 1945.

questions.explanation: Marx inherited concepts from Adam Smith and David Ricardo, then drew very different conclusions.
